Anna, 33, from southeast China's Fujian Province, takes a more old-school approach with a modern media twist. Together, these learners show how English study in China is becoming more visible and social. Instead of presenting fluency as an achievement, these creators use modern entertainment and pop culture to make their learning process watchable, trendy and easy to consume. They prove that language can be practiced, learnt and taught in the middle of ordinary life.
paragraphs.cn: 她有时甚至闭上眼睛，试图记住新闻脚本。除了学习，Anna还为网民提供英语学习服务，使用她的一些方法以及理解式教学，即她朗读场景并提出相关问题。这些学习者共同展示了中国的英语学习正变得更加可见和社交化。这些创作者没有将流利呈现为一种成就，而是利用现代娱乐和流行文化，使他们的学习过程变得可观看、时尚且易于消费。他们证明，语言可以在日常生活中练习、学习和教授。

articles.fullText:
English-language learning has taken on a new form for many Chinese online users who have found unique techniques to ace the skill.
On busy city streets, a young girl spots a foreign visitor and begins asking questions in English. The exchange is sweet and unexpectedly fluent, and has her interviewees intrigued. In videos posted on an Instagram account called English with Darcy, and run by her parents, 4-year-old Darcy Phong from central China's Henan Province chats with travelers about daily life, culture and sightseeing, turning public spaces into impromptu classrooms.
With her dad in sight and a camera in hand, Darcy bravely approaches strangers with her signature line, "Hi! I want to talk with you, can you speak English?" and practices her language skills through conversations with them.
More than impressive, her approach is also super cute. Darcy's Instagram page has amassed a following of over 500,000, with commenters impressed by her command of the English language – even more so because of her age. For her, it all started on her computer, where she'd learn on different programs, as well as from watching scenes from English television shows.
That same do-it-yourself spirit runs through Douyin user known as Miss Zhang, from central China's Hunan Province. In her mid-40s, she creates online clips that have drawn attention for her polished British accent. Miss Zhang spent years teaching herself English, imitating lines from popular shows like Downton Abbey and delighting viewers with her London-style rhythm and intonation.
She is more than happy to share her learning method too, which she says is pretty straight forward: Through watching British dramas on screen, placing highlighted vocabulary notes around the house and rehearsing the words, and doing poetry recitations. In fact, many have been so impressed by her skills, accent and way of speech that she's been overwhelmed with messages and interview requests – she's even had to take a break from posting.
"I could have risen to great fame and fortune instantly, yet I'm a simple, stubborn person, living a free, quiet and solitary life. And those worldly trivialities and social niceties just suffocate me, so I cut off all contact with the outside world and stopped posting," she posted to her Douyin page in July. "Now the buzz has finally faded, so I'm back to making my laid-back clips." She assures her followers that she's going to continue doing what she loves, one British drama at a time.
For Lindsay, from south China's Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the classroom incorporates modern technology in the form of an AI chatbot. Her Douyin profile frames her as an ordinary learner sharing English study, vlogs and life updates.
In one post, she explains that without a foreign teacher or practice partner, she uses AI to rehearse spoken English, asking it to slow down, keep the conversation going and correct her mistakes. Her prompts are practical and specific, covering daily topics, questions in the style of the International English Language Testing System, beginner-friendly exchanges and even conversations around the foods she enjoys eating.
Online users in China are proving that learning English can be done in unique and creative ways, beyond traditional studying from textbooks. 
Anna, 33, from southeast China's Fujian Province, takes a more old-school approach with a modern media twist. She studies and teaches through dictation, memorization and English news reading, using none other than CGTN reports as her material of choice.
Her approach is based on dictation exercises as a way to improve listening, spelling, grammar and vocabulary, formal register and varied sentence structures. She even closes her eyes in some instances in an attempt to memorize news scripts. Beyond just learning, Anna offers services to online users to help them learn English too, using some of her methods as well as comprehension-style teaching where she reads scenarios and offers questions based on these.
Together, these learners show how English study in China is becoming more visible and social. Instead of presenting fluency as an achievement, these creators use modern entertainment and pop culture to make their learning process watchable, trendy and easy to consume. They prove that language can be practiced, learnt and taught in the middle of ordinary life.

articles.fullText:
Editor's note: This series explores how the Ebola outbreak is affecting communities in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo. In this exclusive episode, CGTN Africa takes you inside Mongbwalu, where residents and health workers are confronting the outbreak and working to contain its spread.
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is expanding its Ebola response as health workers confront a surge in suspected infections and the demands of containing the virus in communities.
At Mongbwalu General Hospital in Ituri province, medical teams are treating patients while also monitoring contacts, conducting surveillance and identifying possible new infections.
The added responsibilities are placing pressure on frontline staff, who must often provide care beyond their usual duties.
"When a patient is brought to me without an accompanying person, I have to play two roles: providing care and supervising the patient," head nurse at Mongbwalu General Hospital, Heritier Kumburi Ngabu, said.
"I have to change their clothes, make sure they behave properly in their beds, and take care of them. It's difficult and it weighs on me, but it's our mission, and we're doing our best," he said.
The government and international partners are expanding the hospital's Ebola treatment center to allow suspected cases to be isolated and treated more quickly.
The center currently has 113 beds, while a second facility is under construction.
"Anyone who has been in contact with patients is monitored closely. The moment a contact shows symptoms, they are classified as a suspected case and transferred to the treatment center," said medical doctor Richard Lopayi.
But treatment capacity alone cannot stop transmission, health workers say. Patients must also seek care quickly and communities must cooperate with disease surveillance efforts.
"If someone falls ill, decides to stay home, and refuses to come to the treatment center, they may later die in the community and could have infected dozens of people. When that happens, it becomes harder to break the chain of transmission," Lopayi added.
Health workers are also having to protect themselves from infection while caring for patients and carrying out surveillance.
Since it was officially declared, the Bundibugyo strain has spread faster than any of the DR Congo's previous 16 Ebola outbreaks, according to health authorities.
Frontline workers remain central to the response, but say sustained support from the government and humanitarian partners is needed as authorities work to contain the outbreak.
articles.fullTextCn:
编者按：本系列探讨埃博拉疫情如何影响刚果民主共和国东部社区。在本期独家报道中，CGTN非洲频道带您走进蒙布瓦卢，当地居民和卫生工作者正面对疫情并努力遏制其传播。随着卫生工作者应对疑似感染病例激增以及控制病毒在社区传播的需求，刚果民主共和国正在扩大其埃博拉应对措施。在伊图里省的蒙布瓦卢综合医院，医疗团队在治疗患者的同时，也在监测接触者、进行监测并识别可能的新感染病例。新增的职责给一线工作人员带来了压力，他们往往必须承担超出常规职责的护理工作。蒙布瓦卢综合医院的护士长赫里蒂埃·昆布里·恩加布说：“当病人被送到我这里而没有陪同人员时，我必须扮演两个角色：提供护理和监督病人。”

他说：“我必须给他们换衣服，确保他们在床上表现良好，并照顾他们。这很困难，让我感到沉重，但这是我们的使命，我们正在尽最大努力。”政府和国际合作伙伴正在扩建医院的埃博拉治疗中心，以便疑似病例能更快地被隔离和治疗。该中心目前有113张病床，而第二个设施正在建设中。医疗医生理查德·洛帕伊说：“任何与患者有过接触的人都会被密切监测。一旦接触者出现症状，他们就被归类为疑似病例，并被转移到治疗中心。”

但卫生工作者表示，仅靠治疗能力无法阻止传播。患者还必须迅速寻求护理，社区必须配合疾病监测工作。洛帕伊补充说：“如果有人生病，决定待在家里，拒绝来治疗中心，他们可能会在社区中死亡，并可能感染数十人。当这种情况发生时，打破传播链就变得更加困难。”卫生工作者在照顾患者和进行监测的同时，还必须保护自己免受感染。据卫生当局称，自正式宣布以来，本迪布焦型毒株的传播速度超过了刚果（金）此前16次埃博拉疫情中的任何一次。

一线工作人员仍然是应对措施的核心，但他们表示，在当局努力控制疫情的过程中，需要政府和人道主义伙伴的持续支持。

paragraphs.en:
/CMG
In 1958, Wang was put in charge of a {{11}} rocket program despite having no previous experience in rocketry. Two years later, his team launched the T-7M {{12}} sounding rocket from the {{13}} of Shanghai. He went on to lead the development of more sounding rockets, building China's early launch {{14}}. Wang helped China become the fifth nation to {{15}} launch a satellite when he developed the {{16}} plan for Long March 1, the rocket that carried China's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, into {{17}} in April 1970. Wang Xiji {{18}} with {{19}} in front of the return {{20}} of the Shenzhou-5 spacecraft.

/CMG
1958年，尽管没有火箭技术方面的经验，王希季仍被委以负责探空火箭项目。两年后，他的团队在上海郊区发射了T-7M实验性探空火箭。他继续领导了更多探空火箭的研发，建立了中国早期的发射能力。当王希季为长征一号制定了技术方案，该火箭于1970年4月将中国第一颗卫星东方红一号送入轨道，帮助中国成为第五个独立发射卫星的国家。王希季在神舟五号飞船返回舱前与航天员合影。

中华人民共和国成立后，他放弃了攻读博士学位的计划，于1950年回到中国。王希季坐在办公室里，桌上放着技术文件。/CMG

articles.fullText:
Wang Xiji, a pioneer of China's space program and recipient of the "Two Bombs, One Satellite" Meritorious Service Medal, has died at the age of 105. 
Wang Xiji, a pioneering Chinese space scientist who helped lay the foundations of the country's early rocket and satellite programs, died in Beijing on August 12 at the age of 105.
Wang was one of 23 scientists awarded China's "Two Bombs, One Satellite" Meritorious Service Medal in 1999, a national honor recognizing major contributions to the country's early nuclear, missile and satellite programs.
His career spanned several of China's early space milestones.
Wang Xiji inspects the installation of components inside a recoverable satellite. /CMG
In 1958, Wang was put in charge of a sounding rocket program despite having no previous experience in rocketry. Two years later, his team launched the T-7M experimental sounding rocket from the outskirts of Shanghai. He went on to lead the development of more sounding rockets, building China's early launch capabilities.
Wang helped China become the fifth nation to independently launch a satellite when he developed the technical plan for Long March 1, the rocket that carried China's first satellite, Dongfanghong-1, into orbit in April 1970.
Wang Xiji poses with astronauts in front of the return capsule of the Shenzhou-5 spacecraft. /CMG
He also served as chief designer of China's first recoverable satellite, which launched in November 1975 and returned to Earth with remote-sensing images. China joined the Soviet Union and the United States in mastering satellite recovery technology. The basic design Wang helped establish remained the foundation of China's recoverable satellites for decades.
His path into space technology wasn't direct. He went to the United States in 1948 to study power and fuel engineering at Virginia Polytechnic Institute, earning a master's degree the following year. After the founding of the People's Republic of China, he gave up plans to pursue a doctorate and returned to China in 1950.
Wang Xiji sits at his desk with technical documents in his office. /CMG
His later work extended into crewed spaceflight, small satellites, and long-term space development. Even in his later years, Wang remained involved in discussions on China's lunar exploration and space station programs.
Reflecting on his decades in the field, Wang once described the role he hoped to play simply: "I am willing to be a paving stone to space."

articles.fullText:
Chinese AI models have taken the top five spots in weekly token usage, according to latest data from OpenRouter, a global large-language model (LLM) aggregation leaderboard.
From July 28 to August 3, AI models worldwide processed 56.8 trillion tokens. Chinese models accounted for 28.13 trillion tokens, compared with 4.38 trillion for US models. That's 14 weeks in a row that China has held the lead.
Nine of the world's top 10 most-used models last week were Chinese. DeepSeek's V4-Flash topped rankings with 7.1 trillion tokens in weekly usage, followed by Xiaomi's MiMo-V2.5 with 5.4 trillion, Tencent's Hy3 with 4.89 trillion, DeepSeek's V4-Pro with 3.1 trillion and Z.AI's GLM-5.2 with 2.87 trillion.
Cost comparison
DeepSeek V4-Flash charges $0.14 per million input tokens and $0.28 per million output tokens. Artificial Analysis pegs its average cost at 3 cents per test, compared with 86 cents for Moonshot's Kimi K3, $1.86 for OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol and $3.15 for Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.
The comparison provides a more realistic measure of value than pricing alone because it accounts for the amount of data a model must process and generate to complete a task. A model with low headline price can still prove expensive if it requires significantly more steps to produce an answer.
On the Intelligence Index, DeepSeek V4-Flash scored 50 out of 100, level with Google's Gemini 3.6 Flash, and one point behind Meta's Muse Spark 1.1 and Z.AI's GLM-5.2. Moonshot's Kimi K3 scored 57 while Anthropic's Claude Opus 5, Fable 5 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 scored nine or more points higher.
Artificial Analysis uses a nine-benchmark framework spanning coding, reasoning and workplace-style assignments, to compile model scorecards.
What's given DeepSeek an edge in the global developer market is engineering: better inference, dynamic KV caching, traffic scheduling and long-context optimization.
More overseas companies are integrating DeepSeek APIs, while more international developers are adopting its platform.
Separately on Monday, Alibaba unveiled its largest and most capable AI model to date, the Qwen3.8-Max, which is not far behind in size when compared with an offering from domestic rival Moonshot AI launched last month.
For millions of AI developers worldwide, the shift is already becoming clear: more choices, lower costs and fewer barriers to innovation are reshaping the global AI ecosystem.

paragraphs.en: The Nvidia logo appears on a smartphone screen, with a stock exchange curve chart displayed as the background on a laptop computer screen in this photo illustration in Athens, Greece, on May 21, 2026. Nvidia has partnered with six major financial institutions to launch financing platforms aimed at {{0}} more than $500 billion in third-party capital for artificial intelligence (AI) {{1}}. The chipmaker said on Monday it had signed {{2}} of understanding with Apollo Global Management, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR. The platforms are designed to help AI developers, enterprises, governments and cloud providers finance access to Nvidia-based computing infrastructure as demand for AI computing capacity continues to {{3}}. Under the model, customers could tap {{4}} credit, insurance capital and private funds to finance data centers and computing equipment rather than relying entirely on their own {{5}} sheets. articles.fullText:
The Nvidia logo appears on a smartphone screen, with a stock exchange curve chart displayed as the background on a laptop computer screen in this photo illustration in Athens, Greece, on May 21, 2026. 
Nvidia has partnered with six major financial institutions to launch financing platforms aimed at mobilizing more than $500 billion in third-party capital for artificial intelligence (AI) infrastructure.
The chipmaker said on Monday it had signed memorandums of understanding with Apollo Global Management, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield Asset Management, Goldman Sachs and KKR.
The platforms are designed to help AI developers, enterprises, governments and cloud providers finance access to Nvidia-based computing infrastructure as demand for AI computing capacity continues to surge.
Under the model, customers could tap institutional credit, insurance capital and private funds to finance data centers and computing equipment rather than relying entirely on their own balance sheets.
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said the approach reflects a broader shift in how investors view AI computing infrastructure.
"This is really the first time that technology chips have become an investable asset class," Huang told CNBC. "These are revenue-generating assets now. They're productive, they're long-lived, they're fungible, they're flexible."
The push comes as major technology companies continue to pour hundreds of billions of dollars into AI infrastructure. Their combined spending is expected to exceed $730 billion this year, according to Reuters.
Nvidia said the financing platforms would create dedicated pools of capital for customers as companies and governments race to secure the computing power needed to train and run increasingly advanced AI models.
The initiative could also broaden funding channels for the AI buildout, as large asset managers and private capital firms increasingly seek exposure to digital infrastructure and technology companies face growing scrutiny over the cost and returns of their AI spending.
The $500 billion figure represents a target for capital to be mobilized rather than funding already committed. Nvidia has not disclosed financial terms, individual investment commitments, or a timetable for deploying the planned capital.
